title: Start Here Yoga
paragraphs: This flow is best done daily, and it only takes a few minutes to complete. It is the single best way I know to start the habit of yoga. It gets right to the core — awakening and loosening up the middle of the body and the spine.
practice: Choose a comfortable place to begin. Name one small action in your AI project, such as opening a draft or writing a first prompt. Do that action, then decide what comes next.
reflection: What made beginning feel manageable?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Eyes
paragraphs: This flow is best done whenever you feel stress in and around the eyes. Looking at a computer screen for many hours can be quite taxing on the eyes. This flow is designed to help loosen up the muscles around the eyes and help your eyes relax.
practice: Pause your screen task and let your attention rest on an ordinary detail in your surroundings. Return when you are ready, or finish the session for now.
reflection: What did you notice when you looked away from the task?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Face
paragraphs: Our face is how we greet the world, and it is also subject to a tremendous amount of stress. So much stress and tension is stored in the face. Similar to reflexology with the hands and feet, there is a fractaling effect. Stress in the face will fractal out and effect all of the body. If you look into it, certain parts of the face are connected to certain parts of the body. The same goes for the hands and feet in reflexology. It is truly fascinating. This flow is meant to release tension from the face and have you smiling from feeling better.
practice: Notice your expression without trying to change it. Before sending an AI-assisted message, read it once for tone and choose one detail that expresses your intention.
reflection: How did you want the message to feel to its reader?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Hands
paragraphs: Like the eyes, the hands can be subject to tremendous tension and stress. I know personally that if I work for too long on my laptop — especially typing — I may start to feel tension in the outsides of my hands (by the pinky finger and ring finger). It can quickly become a hindrance. This flow will give your hands some self-care and a nice release of tension. You will be feeling good and ready to get back to work.
practice: Set down your typing task for a moment. Notice where your hands comfortably rest, if that is accessible to you. Choose whether to resume, change the task, or pause.
reflection: What helped you decide whether to continue?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Forearms
paragraphs: The forearms can get really tight from working on a computer. This flow is designed to help you release tension and stress from the forearms so that you can feel better. It is broken up into two parts, with some more advanced exercises at the end of the video.
practice: Before another round of typing, check whether your materials and supports are comfortable to use. Make one ordinary adjustment if useful, then choose a small next task.
reflection: Which adjustment made the work easier to approach?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Elbows
paragraphs: Joints can be tricky, and the elbows are no exception. In this flow, we will work into all the areas around the elbow to promote circulation and healing throughout.
practice: Pause between two AI interactions. Notice one comfortable point of contact with your surroundings. Decide deliberately whether the next interaction is useful right now.
reflection: What helped you choose your next action?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Biceps
paragraphs: The biceps can get so tight. If you think about it, your biceps are often passively contracted — or flexed — when you are working on a computer. Look at the arms. They are at a right angle. The same dynamic happens with the hamstrings in the seated position. This flow will open up the biceps and counterbalance the load from many hours spent on a computer.
practice: Look at how your working space supports you. Rearrange one item if that would help your comfort, or take a break from the task before returning.
reflection: What did you notice about the way you had arranged your work?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Shoulders
paragraphs: Sitting at a computer for too long can cause serious damage to the shoulders. More often than not, the shoulders round and the front body collapses in on itself. We have talked about how on a more subtle level, this is a strong signal to activate the fight-or-flight response. On a more obvious and visual note, the position creates immense strain on the body — especially the shoulders and neck. This yoga flow opens the front body and loosens up the shoulders.
practice: Leave a clear place to resume your project. Take a pause in a supported position that feels comfortable to you. When you return, read that reminder before starting again.
reflection: What made returning to the project simpler?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Neck
paragraphs: People can experience tremendous discomfort and tension in the neck. I am not assigning any blame, but a lot of it can be the result of poor sitting habits. The farther forward your head goes, the heavier it becomes to support. This flow will help correct alignment, and it will have your neck feeling better.
practice: Check whether you can read and use your screen comfortably. Adjust its position or your materials if useful. Name your next task before continuing.
reflection: What helped you work with more ease?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for the Spine
paragraphs: It is said in Eastern culture that you are only as healthy as your spine is flexible. The spine is the core of the body, and it is very important. Further, the modern day spine takes a beating these days through poor sitting habits. This flow is designed to move the spine in all four major directions (or six, depending on how you look at it) — extension, flexion, lateral movement, and rotational movement. Lateral and rotational movement can each be counted twice for left and right.
practice: Consider the sequence of your AI session: arriving, creating, checking, and closing. Choose the part you are in now and one action that belongs to it.
reflection: Where did a clear sequence help you?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Hips
paragraphs: The hips can get extremely tight and locked up through a sedentary lifestyle. In the typical seated position of modern day times, the hips are in a flexed position for nearly the entire day. This is not balanced, and any imbalance in the body eventually leads to problems. If the hips are in flexion most of the day from sitting, we need to intentionally incorporate more hip extension into our lives to balance everything out.
practice: Pause in your usual comfortable working position. Consider whether a change of activity would be welcome. Choose an accessible break or a smaller next step.
reflection: What helped you notice the need for a change?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Lower Back
paragraphs: Lower back pain is a common complaint nowadays. It is never just one thing, but a lot of lower back pain comes from a sedentary lifestyle and too much sitting. Muscular imbalances create problems. Many people do not realize that weak glutes and tight hips almost always lead directly to lower back pain!
practice: Save your work and name the next step. Choose whether to continue in a comfortable supported position, change activity, or finish for now.
reflection: What made it easier to leave the work at a useful stopping point?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Front Body
paragraphs: It is common for a person to have a weak back body and a tight front body nowadays. This is not a good combination, and it leads to poor posture, lower back pain, neck pain, increased stress, and many other problems. Any imbalance in the body and mind eventually leads to issues. This flow is designed to simultaneously strengthen the back body and open the front body for greater overall balance.
poses: Reclined Heart Opener or Assisted Bridge
practice: Notice how your space supports the work you want to do. Make one ordinary adjustment to your surroundings, then begin a task that fits your current attention.
reflection: How did the workspace affect your choice of task?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Balance
paragraphs: Balance is the best thing I know to improve the mind-body connection and proprioception — awareness of where we are in space. It is also a highly effective present moment vehicle — metaphorically driving you right into the now, bringing you fully into the body. Balance is essential, and it is also vital for injury prevention. Don’t ever get intimidated by having poor balance, and don’t get frustrated. Start from where you are, and remember that balance is not binary. It is a spectrum.
practice: Review the balance between creating and checking in your AI project. Choose one result to verify, or one small idea to develop, depending on what the work needs.
reflection: Which side of the work needed more attention?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Relaxation
paragraphs: This flow is best done later in the day or just prior to sleep. It can also be utilized if you are ever feeling anxious or stressed out. We will be staying in poses slightly longer and really emphasizing deep breathing.
practice: Save a short note about where to resume. Step away from the current task for a pause that suits you. You can return afterward or deliberately close the session.
reflection: What did you want to leave for your future self?
note: This source page is a flow overview and pose inventory, rather than complete step-by-step instruction. The new application below is an attention or work exercise, separate from the physical sequence.

title: Yoga for Energy
paragraphs: This yoga flow is best done early in the day or whenever you are feeling lethargic. It is designed to help wake you up and get everything flowing.
practice: Notice the attention and capacity you have today. Choose a task small enough to approach now, or choose a pause. If you begin, complete one manageable action before expanding it.
reflection: Which task fit the capacity you had?

title: Meditation for Focus
paragraphs: Find a comfortable seated position, or relax down on your back. First, with the eyes open, fix your gaze on an external focus point — anything will work. Maybe it is a painting or a picture? It could be a tree outside your window, or a spot on the wall. It doesn’t matter what you pick, but it does matter that you pick something. Don’t try to pierce the focus point with your eyes, but rather soften your gaze. As you continue to focus on this external point, begin to take low and slow deep breaths — in and out through the nose; expanding the belly.

Don’t worry about blinking too much, and don’t worry about messing anything up. Let all of the mind chatter go. Focus only on the point as you continue to breathe deeply. If your mind wanders off, gently bring it back to the focus point.
Several Deep Breaths

Now, I invite you to close the eyes — internalizing our awareness and our focus point. Let’s bring all of our focus to the breath. It is our new focus point although internal and invisible. Anytime the mind drifts away, bring it back to the breath. Additionally, we are trying to make each breath the best breath possible. Nothing else matters. Nothing else exists.
Several Deep Breaths

This is the practice of yoga. It is the practice of mastering focus. The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali clearly says that this is what the system of yoga is designed to do. Mastering focus is the most effective way to heal the mind and enrich your life, as well as how to achieve greatness. Never forget how essential focus is, and never allow your focus to be hijacked. Do not allow it to atrophy. Instead, workout your focus like you would do with a muscle.
Several Deep Breaths

You workout your focus by bringing it to one point. The more often and the more intensely you bring your focus to one point, the stronger your focus will become. The stronger you will become. Every time you bring the focus to a single point and hold it there, you are practicing meditation. It is the true definition of meditation according to the 8 Petals of Yoga.
Several Deep Breaths
You have just dialed in your focus for the rest of the day. Take a few more deep breaths, then end this meditation whenever you are ready.
practice: Choose one comfortable point of attention: a sound, a visible detail, or your natural breath. Notice it briefly without forcing your breathing or gaze. When your attention wanders, return gently, then choose one small AI task.
reflection: What helped you return to the point you chose?
note: The original includes directed breathing and broad claims about focus. The new application uses a comfortable point of attention and natural breathing, without promising a particular outcome.

title: Meditation for Innovation
paragraphs: Find a comfortable seat, or relax down on your back. Release everything that is not now. I invite you to close the eyes and connect with your breath. Let’s take some big deep breaths — in and out through the nose; low and slow from the belly. We are slowing the breath down as much as we can, and we are expanding the breath as much as possible.
Several Deep Breaths

Innovation is in the air. The answers you are looking for are available to you, however we often block the answers with our own biases and beliefs. I am not asking you to change your beliefs, and I know it takes time to clear cognitive biases, however for the next few minutes, let’s do an experiment. For just the next few minutes, let’s empty as much as possible. There is no need to fear anything being lost forever. I promise it will still be there after this meditation. However, for just the next few minutes, let go of everything.
Several Deep Breaths

Let go of your job title. Let go of all your likes and dislikes. Let go of how you think things should be. Let go of absolutely everything — including your identity. Be humble and open. Know that the answers you are looking for are available. Innovation is in the air. Invite it in.
Several Deep Breaths

Too often, we get in our own way in life. Too often, our biases and beliefs blind us to the truth, as well as to the answers we are looking for. Embrace the crystal mind of yoga. Let go of attachments and empty as much as possible. Stay humble and stay open. Invite innovation in. Take a few more deep breaths, then end this meditation whenever you are ready.
practice: Choose a creative question. Write down one assumption you are making, then invite an alternative approach from your AI tool. Compare the options with your purpose and check what matters before choosing.
reflection: Which assumption became easier to reconsider?
note: The source’s crystal-mind and identity imagery is a philosophical framework. The new application explores one creative assumption without asking you to surrender your identity or force your breathing.

title: Meditation on Mortality
paragraphs: Find a comfortable seated position, or relax down on your back. Take a big exhalation — releasing everything that is not here and now. I invite you to close the eyes, bringing your awareness to the breath. Let’s take some big deep breaths — in and out through the nose; low and slow from the belly.
Several Deep Breaths

I want to warn you that this can be a very intense meditation. It can be absolutely terrifying to look death in the eye, however the benefits of doing so are immense. On the other side of this meditation is more love and more beauty than you can imagine. Let’s do several more deep breaths.
Several Deep Breaths

Now, I want you to imagine the person you love most in this world. It doesn’t literally have to be the number one person, but it can be one of the people you love the most. Clearly see this person in your mind’s eye. Take a few moments and a few breaths to see some of the things you’ve done with this person.
Several Deep Breaths

Now that you have imagined a person you deeply love in this world, imagine a world without this person. Imagine that you wake up tomorrow and you find out this person has died. I know this is intense, but there is a purpose, and this is for good reason. With this person you love now being gone, do any of those small annoyances matter anymore? Do any of the arguments matter anymore? What would you give to be able to spend another day with this person? How would you act if you knew tomorrow would be the last day with your loved one? What would you say? What wouldn’t you say? Let’s take several more deep breaths.
Several Deep Breaths

This meditation has the power to erase all negativity. When you know it may be the last time with someone, you act differently. You care more. You love more. You are more present, and there is more beauty. Let’s do the same thing with someone who is currently annoying you, frustrating you, or stressing you out. Clearly see this person in your mind’s eye. Next, imagine you wake up tomorrow and this person has died. Would you still be frustrated? Would you still be annoyed? Does this put things into perspective? How would you act if you knew tomorrow would be your last interaction with this person? What would you say? What wouldn’t you say? Let’s take several more deep breaths.
Several Deep Breaths

For the last part of this meditation, I want to go even deeper. Let’s imagine that you wake up and find out you have died. You are out of body, looking down at your own funeral. How many people would be there? Who would be there? What would people say about you? You don’t have forever, and you never know when your last day will be. What would your funeral be like if you were to die tomorrow? Let’s do some more deep breaths.
Several Deep Breaths

If you made it this far into the meditation, I want to commend you. This is not easy. Even though death is the only guarantee in life and literally everyone dies, it is still so difficult to talk about. You may not be feeling the benefits yet, but I want you to notice how your relationships and interactions with people change. When you treat each moment with a person as if it could be the last one, all negativity is instantly erased. The presence is palpable, and the beauty is amplified beyond belief. The power of this meditation lies in the truth of it. I’ve learned this lesson the hard way twice, and it is my wish that you don’t have to. Treat every interaction with a person as if it could be the last one, because it very well might be.
practice: If you wish, think of someone or something you value in your life today. Without imagining a loss, choose one small act of attention or care you can offer while keeping your boundaries. You may skip this reflection.
reflection: What deserves a little of your attention today?
note: This original script includes vivid imagery of the deaths of loved ones and your own funeral. You can skip the original and use the optional reflection below, which focuses on present-day care without death imagery. It does not ask you to erase feelings or forgive someone.

title: Thank You Love Meditation
paragraphs: This is my personal favorite and absolute go-to meditation. It centers me and invites in good energy. Life is not always simple, but gratitude and love are often a good response to nearly all situations. Although this meditation can be done anywhere at any time, let’s start by finding a comfortable seated position, or relax down on the back.
Let go of everything that is not now. Allow it to dissolve on a big exhalation. Let’s take some big deep belly breaths — low and slow; in and out through the nose.
Several Deep Breaths

Next, let’s sync up mantra with breath. On inhalation, repeat “thank you” silently within. Briefly hold on fullness. Then, on exhalation, repeat “I love you” silently within, with a brief hold on emptiness. Let’s repeat this several times.
Several Deep Breaths

You can apply this to anyone and anything. You can add the name of a loved one after “thank you” and “I love you”, or another’s name — including your own. This will not only focus the mind, but it will dissolve negativity and amplify beauty. Let’s do some deep breaths practicing this — repeating “thank you” on the inhalation and “I love you” on the exhalation.
Several Deep Breaths
Let’s now practice with various objects — gross (obvious) and subtle. Here are some examples.
Thank you, nature. I love you, nature.
Thank you, water. I love you, water.
Thank you, AI. I love you, AI.
These are just a few examples. Use your own as we do several more deep belly breaths.
Several Deep Breaths

You can be as specific or as expansive as you want with this. You can use this for a specific meal, or thank the entire world. Find what works best for you. You’ll notice certain phrases really shift your energy in a positive way. I call these power mantras. Practice a few more deep breaths, using mantra variations of choice, then end this meditation whenever you are ready.
practice: If gratitude feels appropriate, name one specific thing you appreciate. You may recall the words ‘thank you’ or choose words of your own. Let your breath remain natural, without holding it or requiring a positive feeling.
reflection: What did you appreciate, and how might you express it?
note: The source includes breath holds and promises about negativity and well-being. The new application uses optional words of appreciation, with natural breathing and no holds or required emotional response.
